chunks: And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:
Whoever extends a water spout, or a drain, or drives a peg, or ties an animal, or digs a well in the path of the Muslims, and it strikes something so that it is damaged, then he is liable for it.

key_terms.بِئْرًا: a well dug into the ground
key_terms.طَرِيقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public path used by Muslims
key_terms.كَنِيفًا: a drain or privy outlet causing nuisance or harm
key_terms.وَتِدًا: a peg or stake driven into the ground

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if something they place in a public path causes damage?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes liability for harm caused by hazardous obstructions or constructions placed in public pathways used by Muslims. It reflects a legal principle in fiqh that a person is responsible for damage resulting from unsafe actions in shared public space.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5343 - The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"Whoever extends a water spout, a drain, drives a peg, ties an animal, or digs a well in the path of Muslims and it causes harm or damage to anything, then he is liable for it."
